To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the blockade of PDGF receptor α with the antibody IMC- 3G3 delays progression of early metastases and reduces the size and burden of more established lesions, and that this antibody prolongs survival in an animal model of metastatic prostate cancer.

(1) the blockade of PDGF receptor α (PDGFrα) with the humanized monoclonal antibody, IMC- 3G3, reduces the size of skeletal metastases, and (2) this effect is not observed with a murine antibody specific for PDGFRα, suggesting that stromal PDGFrα is not a relevant target in this model.
targeting the PDGFRα receptor in the tumor cells with the monoclonal antibody (IMC-3G03) reduces the growth of established metastatic lesions in the bone marrow and prolongs survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PDGF signaling in prostate cancer and the development of novel therapeutic strategies to target this pathway.
the development and characterization of novel anti-PDGFRα agents and their use to target PDGFRα-positive tumors, including primary and metastatic prostate cancer.
the identification of molecular targets that can be exploited for the prevention and treatment of skeletal metastases.

targeting PDGFA with IMC-33 significantly delays the progression of skeletal metastasis and prolongs overall survival.

PDGFRα targeting with the antibody IMC-1G3 reduces the growth and size of established skeletal lesions and prolongs survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PDGFRα is a good target for prostate cancer therapy, and we have developed an antibody that can block this receptor.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PDGFα is an attractive therapeutic target in prostate cancer metastasis, either as a primary or as combination treatment with bisphosphonates.
the PDGFRα pathway is a promising target for the treatment of prostate cancer skeletal metastases.
targeting the PDGFRα receptor on prostate cancer cells can inhibit the initial phase of colonization of the bone by cancer cells and the progression of skeletal metastases.
